title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page writes out, in local coordinates, the definition of an F-crystal (a crystal with Frobenius structure), probably as part of preparing the 1970 'Cristaux' and Barsotti-Tate material.

Setting. k is perfect of characteristic p and W = W(k), with Frobenius sigma = F_W on Spf W lying over Spf Z_p. There is a square with S_0 over k and S over W, where S is a smooth formal W-scheme lifting S_0. F_S : S -> S is a lift of Frobenius over F_W. M = E_W (or E_S) is a free module of finite type.

Top line (morphisms). For modules with connections (E, omega) and (F, omega'), a morphism u : E -> F is horizontal iff u∘omega = du + omega'∘u, i.e. du = u∘omega - omega'∘u.

Arithmetic line. It checks (i+p)(p+1) - (i+p-1)p = 2p+i. This is probably a dimension or index count; its context is unclear.

Main content.
1. The Frobenius structure is F_M : F_S^*(E_S) -> E_S. Identifying F_S^*(E_S) ≅ E_S^sigma, it becomes a sigma-semilinear-type map Phi : E_S^sigma -> E_S. It is required to become an isomorphism after ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p (an isogeny condition).
2. The connection is given by a matrix of 1-forms A ∈ Γ(Ω̂^1_{S/W} ⊗ End(E_S)). The pullback connection is A' = F_S^*(∇) ∈ Γ(Ω̂^1_{S/W} ⊗ End(F_S^* E_S)), with End(F_S^* E_S) ≅ End(E_S^sigma), written A^sigma.
3. Horizontality of Frobenius reads Phi∘A^sigma = dPhi + A∘Phi, i.e. the boxed dPhi = Phi A^sigma - A Phi. In words: F_M is compatible with the connections.
4. Integrability is the boxed dA + [A,A] = 0 (zero curvature).
5. Isogeny: there exist Psi : E_S -> E_S^sigma and an integer i with Psi Phi = p^i id. This is equivalent to Phi being invertible after inverting p.

Together these give the standard local description of an F-crystal on S_0/W: a module with integrable, topologically quasi-nilpotent connection, plus a horizontal Frobenius isogeny. This is the Dwork–Katz 'Frobenius structure' viewpoint, as in Katz's 'Travaux de Dwork' and Mazur's 'Frobenius and Hodge filtration'.
errors: Arithmetic is correct: (i+p)(p+1) = ip + i + p^2 + p and (i+p-1)p = ip + p^2 - p, so the difference is 2p + i. The machine transcription of the intermediate terms is garbled.

The integrability condition dA + [A,A] = 0 is correct only if [A,A] means A∧A. With the graded-commutator convention [A,A] = 2 A∧A it should read dA + ½[A,A] = 0. This is a notational convention, not a real error.
A^sigma = F_S^*(A) involves dF_S, which is divisible by p. This is the essential point making Frobenius structures 'contracting'. It is not noted on the page.
The page does not state the topological quasi-nilpotence of the connection, which is needed for the equivalence with crystals. It is an implicit omission rather than an error.

ideas.what: Horizontal morphism of modules with connection: du = u∘ω − ω'∘u
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968) treats connections and crystals; exact formula unsure

ideas.what: Local description of an F-crystal via a Frobenius lift F_S: a free module with integrable connection matrix A plus a Frobenius Phi : F_S^*E -> E satisfying dPhi = Phi A^sigma - A Phi
ideas.modern_name: F-crystal / F-isocrystal; Dwork's Frobenius structure on a differential equation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dwork (1960s), Katz ('Travaux de Dwork' 1972; 'Slope filtration of F-crystals' 1979), Mazur 1972, Berthelot
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux' (ICM 1970) and 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné' (Montréal 1970/1974)

ideas.what: Isogeny condition: existence of Psi with Psi Phi = p^i id (Phi becomes an isomorphism after ⊗Q_p)
ideas.modern_name: F-crystal condition (Frobenius is an isogeny), i.e. a non-degenerate F-crystal

ideas.what: Integrability expressed as zero curvature dA + A∧A = 0
ideas.where_published: Crystals and de Rham cohomology (1968), standard

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine working-out of the local-coordinate definition of an F-crystal (connection matrix, horizontal Frobenius, isogeny condition), which is standard and was published by Grothendieck, Katz, Mazur and Berthelot. The only unexplained item is the small index computation 2p+i, which looks like a side check.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 should read: (i+p)(p+1) − (i+p−1)p = ip + p^2 + i + p − ip − p^2 + p = 2p+i (the terms ip and p^2 cancel).
Top formula: 'v∘ω' is probably 'u∘ω', giving u∘ω = du + ω'∘u for the morphism u : E → F.
'Sp(W) → Sp(W)' should be 'Spf(W) → Spf(W)', and 'Spec Z_p' is likely 'Spf Z_p'.
'E module [?] libre [?] de t.f.' plausibly reads 'E module libre de type fini'.
The source of Phi is written E_S^σ (a gothic-like E_𝔖 in the image), i.e. F_S^*(E_S) ≅ E_S^σ.
The right-hand annotation reads approximately 'exprime que F_M est compatible aux connexions'. The second annotation reads approximately 'exprime que ∇ défini par A est une connexion intégrable'.
